column1: # Verbs that take an indirect object written as a + noun phrase: the person
# or thing that receives, is told, is asked or is affected (dar el libro a
# María, telefonear a Juan, gustar a Marco). A dative clitic can stand for it
# or double it (le doy el libro, le di el libro a María, le gusta a Marco).
# Only after these verbs does the grammar read an a phrase as an indirect
# keeps its adverbial reading too (dar el libro a la salida), so a sentence
# where both fit is ambiguous. A place after a verb of motion (ir a Madrid),
# the personal a of a direct object (ver a María), a + infinitive and a + que
# are not indirect objects. ir is left out on purpose: its dative sense
# (le voy al Barça, "I support") is rare beside ir a + place.
# One verb per line as the infinitive, then where the evidence comes from,
# then for model-proposed verbs an example phrase:
#   wiktionary-sense    a sense note "[with dative]", "[with a 'someone']",
#                       "(uses indirect object)" or the like in English
#                       verbs), where the a phrase is one a dative clitic can
#   wiktionary-example  a Wiktionary usage example with le / les + the verb +
#                       a + a person or thing (le di eso a mi mamá)
#   tatoeba             a sentence of tatoeba-pool.jsonl.gz (which holds
#                       homograph-set.jsonl) with le / les + the verb + a + a
#                       noun phrase as its indirect object
#                       proposed by a language model (Claude Opus), with the
#                       example phrase in the third column, and accepted by a
#                       second, independent model (Claude Sonnet) that saw only
#                       the list and rejected 1 of 86 proposals (2026-11-15)
